text: {"findings":[{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Unsourced churn and cost figures","detail":"The 12% never-reorder rate and the $48M annual cost are stated as fact and attributed only to vague 'industry data'. There is no citation, so the size of the problem cannot be verified.","evidence_quote":"Industry data shows that 12% of customers never reorder after a late delivery, costing roughly $48M a year.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the specific source, or replace the figures with internal LMD data on post-late-delivery reorder rates and the revenue impact."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for credits and retention","detail":"The only guardrail is Cost Per Delivery. A credit program needs guardrails on credit abuse or fraud, such as the claim or credit rate and repeat credit recipients. It also needs a guardrail on the on-time rate, since credits may reduce the incentive to improve, and on order and margin economics.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: stop if it rises by more than $0.15.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for credit redemption and abuse rate, net margin per order, and on-time delivery rate. Add a reorder or retention metric to show that the credits pay for themselves."},{"type":"NO_BASELINE_TARGET","title":"Guardrail has no baseline","detail":"The Cost Per Delivery guardrail states a threshold but no baseline value or measurement window. The $0.15 stop rule cannot be evaluated without them. The success metric is also only CSAT and never measures the reorder behavior named in the problem.","evidence_quote":"Cost Per Delivery: stop if it rises by more than $0.15.","citations":[],"recommendation":"State the current Cost Per Delivery baseline and the measurement window. Add a reorder-rate success metric with a baseline, target and timeframe."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of exposure and mismatch with the target window","detail":"The experiment runs 3 weeks, but the success target is set at 8 weeks, so the test cannot validate it. Late orders are a small subset, so the sample of treated late deliveries in 3 weeks is likely too small for the stated MDE, and no sample size calculation is shown. The next-order credit effect on reorder also needs a longer window.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by customer. Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.15 CSAT points, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align the experiment duration with the target timeframe. Show a sample size calculation based on the volume of late orders, and extend the run to capture the next-order behavior."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Ambiguous CSAT metric name","detail":"'Delivery CSAT on late orders' is a custom, scoped variant, and the scale and survey source are not specified. It may not match a canonical glossary metric.","evidence_quote":"Delivery CSAT on late orders: baseline 3.6, target 3.9 within 8 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use the canonical glossary CSAT metric name and define the scale, the survey response population, and how late orders are filtered."}]}
